A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XTransfer work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching material relocated between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification, blood-pressure estimation, component-ablation, and cloud/edge resource measurements in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds SRR/LWS ablations and a post-hoc compression comparison in Tables 4, 5, and 13.

M1.justification: The SRR pipeline, PCA anchor alignment, repair loss, channel removal, LWS control, and post-fine-tuning procedure are retained. Channel removal moves from v3 Appendix B.2 to v4 Section 4.3. Clarifications about connector initialization and distance computation do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The source and target datasets, sensing modalities, participant coverage, classification tasks, blood-pressure regression task, and device scenarios are retained. The new ablations and compression comparison use existing datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: v4 adds DAPN+Pruning as an evaluated comparator in Appendix C.10 and Table 13. Tables 4–5 also introduce SRR and SRR-w/o-Removal comparison variants. The previously evaluated external baselines remain.

E3.justification: v4 adds controls disabling LWS and channel removal, plus a pruning protocol matching DAPN's average model size to Our-Single separately for each HHAR shot setting. Existing LOOCV, shot settings, and training budgets are retained. ATR's written denominator is corrected without evidence that existing scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's component-level probes, v4 adds end-to-end SRR-versus-LWS ablations across six datasets and three shot settings, measuring both accuracy and ATR. Appendix C.10 also tests whether size-matched conventional compression can reproduce the efficiency benefits. These substantially strengthen analysis of the core stages and an alternative explanation for their gains.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 15 rounds per setting, fixed random seeds, and CUDA convolution determinism. Existing error bars and blood-pressure error statistics are retained; the new tables introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting or statistical-testing practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add cross-dataset accuracy and ATR results for two component variants, and Table 13 adds the pruning results. At 5-shot HHAR, newly reported SRR achieves 61.8% accuracy and 0.55 ATR, while DAPN+Pruning achieves 28.3% and 0.64. Existing Our-Single results remain 71.8% and 1.57; the additions are new result sets rather than improved full-method scores.

T1.justification: v4 corrects ATR's mathematical grouping so both weighted resource terms are inside the denominator, and corrects the accumulated-cost and regression-fit summation indices in Section 5. Other equation changes chiefly clarify notation or display existing mathematics; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusion retain the claims of modality-agnostic few-shot transfer, SRR repairing, efficient LWS recombination, and reduced data/resource costs. The additional evidence does not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 discusses channel removal's less stable accuracy benefits without LWS, connector overhead without structural optimization, and the limitations of post-hoc pruning. The conclusion newly identifies optimal source-model selection as future work. These provide substantive qualifications to the retained method.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 adds code-repository access information. v4 also specifies target-specific connector initialization and Euclidean repair distance, while its Impact Statement documents consent, anonymization, and controlled data sharing. The existing software, hardware, and optimizer details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Gupta et al. (2026), Better Together, to support the intuition that useful cross-modal structure can exist without paired data. The PyTorch Hub and Chen bibliography changes concern existing references rather than new research relationships.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized explanatory edits, promotes channel removal to Section 4.3, revises the Section 6.3 heading, and adds discussion, acknowledgements, and an Impact Statement. The overall narrative order and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: The accuracy and ATR tables gain ablation rows; v3 Appendix Table 12 becomes main-text Table 5; and v4 adds the compression comparison as Table 13. Several equations become displayed equations, with adjustments to Figure 4 spacing and table placement. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added component ablations and size-matched pruning comparison strengthen attribution of accuracy and efficiency gains. Clearer equations, code-access information, and explicit limitations also improve assessability. The gains are limited by remaining overgeneralizations: for example, Table 5 does not support v4's blanket statement that SRR-w/o-Removal has lower ATR than the baselines.
